item.title: Unpatched Windows CLFS zero day exploit SignDrop enables SYSTEM privilege escalation
item.description:
Operating system security researchers have published a zero-day exploit targeting core Windows system log drivers and antimalware components. Local unprivileged users can exploit authentication driver subroutines to execute arbitrary file creation routines and gain full SYSTEM execution privileges on target hosts.
The zero-day exploit, codenamed SignDrop and released by security researcher Nightmare Eclipse, targets the Windows Common Log File System CLFS driver alongside Windows Defender file handling routines. The exploit manipulates CLFS driver authentication modes to force arbitrary file creation under the security context of the antimalware process. Local threat actors exploit the flaw to elevate unprivileged local access to SYSTEM privileges, bypassing endpoint detection barriers and disabling active host defenses. Vendor advisories detail registry mitigation checks while formal security patches remain pending.
Subverting core operating system log drivers and endpoint security daemons destroys local privilege boundaries across corporate host fleets. Because CLFS handles low-level transaction logging across Windows environments, local privilege escalation exploits permit threat actors holding low-privilege initial access to compromise domain endpoints, dump system credentials, and deploy ransomware binaries.
- Inspect Windows registry CLFS authentication mode configuration keys to verify authentication mode settings are enforced. - Restrict unprivileged local account execution privileges and mandate strict application control policies on Windows endpoints. - Monitor endpoint security telemetry for unauthorized file creation calls originating from Windows Defender service daemons. - Enforce strict Endpoint Detection and Response EDR behavioral monitoring around CLFS log file generation subroutines.
Operating system defense demands rigid process integrity validation and continuous local privilege auditing to ensure Windows host fleets remain protected against zero-day driver privilege escalation exploits. #CodeDefence #SignDrop #Windows #ZeroDay #CLFS #PrivilegeEscalation #SYSTEM #EndpointSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Red Hat patches maximum severity CVSS 98 authentication bypass in Quay container registries CVE-2026-123710
item.description:
Container registry infrastructure maintainers have distributed security updates resolving a maximum-severity authentication vulnerability in cloud container storage platforms. Unauthenticated remote adversaries can forge valid access tokens to push and pull container images across any hosted repository.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123710 with a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8, impacts Red Hat Quay container registry deployments. The defect involves improper access token signing key validation during repository authentication handshakes. Unauthenticated remote threat actors add arbitrary public keys to Quay's trusted key store without expiration limits, signing unauthorized access tokens that Quay accepts for any repository. Red Hat released fixed builds across eight Quay 3 branches to resolve the defect.
Subverting enterprise container registries exposes software supply chains to malicious container image tampering and proprietary code theft. Because Quay hosts production container images for cloud-native microservices, unauthenticated image push access allows threat actors to inject backdoors into production deployment images and exfiltrate proprietary code artifacts.
- Apply fixed build updates released across Red Hat Quay 3 branches immediately across all container registry nodes. - Disable anonymous access configurations across public Quay container registry instances if immediate patching cannot be performed. - Audit Quay trusted signing key stores for unauthorized public key entries created during recent operation windows. - Enforce container image signing and image verification pipelines prior to deploying container workloads to production clusters.
Container platform security requires immediate software patch execution and strict repository token verification to ensure cloud deployment pipelines remain protected against unauthenticated image tampering. #CodeDefence #RedHat #Quay #ContainerSecurity #AuthBypass #SupplyChain #CloudSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #DevSecOps

item.title: CISA reaches November 13 federal compliance deadline for Barracuda ESG vulnerabilities CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560
item.description:
Federal civilian executive branch agencies reach today's mandatory compliance deadline under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 to patch or disconnect perimeter email security appliances. Threat actors actively chain authentication bypass logic and command injection errors to obtain unauthenticated root access on target gateways.
The mandatory remediation mandate applies to Barracuda Email Security Gateway ESG vulnerabilities CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560. Threat telemetry confirms threat actors actively weaponize alternate path authentication bypass flaw CVE-2026-116606 alongside timezone parsing command injection bug CVE-2026-111560. By combining both vulnerabilities, remote adversaries achieve unauthenticated root command execution on exposed appliances, deploying persistent web shells and inspecting corporate mail streams. Non-compliant federal endpoints face mandatory network disconnection orders.
Subverting perimeter email inspection appliances undermines organizational communication security and network boundary defense. Because Barracuda ESG appliances inspect incoming enterprise mail streams, enforce anti-phishing controls, and manage transport layer encryption, an unauthenticated root takeover allows threat actors to intercept sensitive emails and pivot into internal subnets.
- Verify mandatory security update deployment across all exposed Barracuda Email Security Gateway appliances immediately. - Execute mandatory forensic triage checks across appliance file systems to inspect for unauthorized web shells or backdoor scripts. - Restrict public internet access to administrative management web interfaces, placing management ports on isolated out-of-band VLANs. - Rotate administrative account credentials and digital certificates configured on managed email inspection appliances.
Perimeter gateway defense requires immediate patch validation and thorough forensic triage auditing to ensure email security appliances remain protected against unauthenticated root takeover chains. #CodeDefence #Barracuda #ESG #CISA #KEV #BOD2604 #AuthBypass #CommandInjection #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement
